title: Septic Arthritis: Joint Aspiration, Antimicrobial Therapy and Surgical Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with an acutely hot, swollen, painful native joint in the emergency department (ED) or primary care: treat as septic until proven otherwise, aspirate before antibiotics, blood cultures, empirical antibiotics including penicillin-allergy and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) options, drainage, and orthopaedic or rheumatology referral. Uses the British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) and British Orthopaedic Association hot-joint guideline summary, the NHS Lothian 2024 antimicrobial guideline and product information. Prosthetic joints are referred directly to orthopaedics; children have their own pathway, but paediatric doses from labels are shown.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi septic arthritis guideline was found.
Only the published summary of the BSR/BOA 2006 guideline was opened, not the full text.
Gentamicin is advised by NHS Lothian for higher Gram-negative risk but dosed by a local calculator; no gentamicin label was opened, so no dose is given.
Gonococcal arthritis treatment is not covered; take samples and discuss with microbiology.
Typical normal ranges for white cells, C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate are not from these sources.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: A short history of a hot, swollen, tender joint with restricted movement should be treated as septic until proven otherwise (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Summary). Likely organisms are Staphylococcus aureus, streptococci, Enterobacteriaceae and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Notes). Pus in the joint must be removed as well as treated with antibiotics (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Drainage). MRSA risk is higher in nursing home residents and recent inpatients; Gram-negative risk in the elderly, frail or immunosuppressed (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Empirical therapy; NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Empirical).

symptoms: Acute hot, swollen, painful joint (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Summary).
Restricted movement (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Summary).
Fever or feeling unwell (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Investigations).
physicalSigns: Tender, swollen, warm joint with reduced range of movement (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Summary).
Effusion that can be aspirated (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Aspiration).
redFlags: Possible prosthetic joint infection: refer to orthopaedics for aspiration (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Aspiration).
Sepsis: blood cultures and antibiotics without delay after samples (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Investigations).

Gram-negative risk factors (elderly, frail, recurrent urinary infection, recent urological or abdominal surgery): discuss early with microbiology (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Empirical).
precipitants: Nursing home residence or recent hospital admission (MRSA risk) (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Empirical therapy).
Older age and immunosuppression (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Empirical therapy).
Recent urological or abdominal surgery (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Empirical).
Sexual exposure for gonococcal arthritis (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Notes).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Crystals on polarising microscopy of synovial fluid; crystals do not exclude infection (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Laboratory).
Sexual risk; chlamydia and gonorrhoea nucleic acid test and joint fluid polymerase chain reaction (PCR) (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Notes).
Joint replacement in situ; orthopaedic aspiration (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Aspiration).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat as septic until proven otherwise
actions: Assess the joint and look for sepsis (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Summary).
Prosthetic joint: refer to orthopaedics for aspiration (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Aspiration).

clinicalManagement.title: Aspirate and culture before antibiotics
actions: Aspirate the joint for Gram stain, culture and crystals (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Sections Aspiration and Laboratory).
Take 2 sets of blood cultures from separate sites (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Investigations).
If gonococcal infection is possible, send NAAT samples (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Notes).

clinicalManagement.title: Start empirical antibiotics
actions: Give an antibiotic active against S. aureus and streptococci (see Medicines) (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Empirical therapy).
Adjust for MRSA or Gram-negative risk with microbiology (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Empirical).

clinicalManagement.title: Drain the joint
actions: Remove pus by repeated needle aspiration or arthroscopic washout; discuss all cases with orthopaedics or rheumatology (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Drainage; NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Warning).

clinicalManagement.title: Complete the course
actions: Intravenous for up to 2 weeks or until improving, then oral for about 4 weeks; NHS Lothian recommends 4 weeks total (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Duration; NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Empirical).
Switch to oral based on microbiology results; consider outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy for stable patients (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Sections Switch and Notes).

regimens.indication: Empirical treatment of native-joint septic arthritis
regimens.dose: Adults: 2 g intravenously every 6 hours (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Empirical); SmPC allows up to 8 g daily in osteomyelitis, maximum 12 g daily (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.2). PAEDIATRIC under 12 years: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in 3 to 4 divided doses, up to 100 mg/kg/day in severe infection, no single dose above 33 mg/kg (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.2).
regimens.route: Intravenous injection over 3 to 4 minutes or infusion over 20 to 30 minutes
regimens.duration: Intravenous up to 2 weeks or until improving, then oral; total about 4 weeks
adjustments: Creatinine clearance below 10 mL/min: reduce dose or extend interval; adult maximum 1 g every 8 to 12 hours (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.2).
No hepatic dose reduction, but use caution in hepatic dysfunction (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Sections 4.2 and 4.4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Liver tests: hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice can appear up to 2 months later, more often over 50 years (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.4).
With paracetamol: watch for high anion gap metabolic acidosis (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.4).
C-reactive protein and clinical response (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Duration).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to flucloxacillin or other beta-lactams (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.3).
Previous flucloxacillin-associated jaundice or hepatic dysfunction (Flucloxacillin SmPC, Section 4.3).

teaching.scope: Adults with an acutely hot, swollen, painful native joint in the emergency department (ED) or primary care: treat as septic until proven otherwise, aspirate before antibiotics, blood cultures, empirical antibiotics including penicillin-allergy and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) options, drainage, and orthopaedic or rheumatology referral. Uses the British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) and British Orthopaedic Association hot-joint guideline summary, the NHS Lothian 2024 antimicrobial guideline and product information. Prosthetic joints are referred directly to orthopaedics; children have their own pathway, but paediatric doses from labels are shown.
learningObjectives: Treat a hot swollen joint as septic until proven otherwise.
Choose flucloxacillin or vancomycin by allergy and MRSA risk.
Drain the joint and plan the course.
pitfalls: Diagnosing gout without Gram stain and culture.
keyPoints: Prosthetic joints go to orthopaedics for aspiration.
Antibiotics alone are not enough; drain the pus.

patientEducation: A joint infection can damage the joint quickly; you need antibiotics for several weeks and the joint may need draining.
Report fever, new swelling or worsening pain.
lifestyleAndDiet: Gentle movement and physiotherapy once infection is controlled.
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; orthopaedics or rheumatology; microbiology; physiotherapy; outpatient parenteral antibiotic team (NHS Lothian septic arthritis 2024, Section Notes).
dischargeCriteria: Joint improving, afebrile, inflammatory markers falling, organism and oral switch agreed, follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Orthopaedic or rheumatology review with inflammatory markers until the course is complete (BSR/BOA hot joint guideline 2006, Section Duration).
